results.headline: Employer of record first, then your own company from month 7
results.reason: From about 6 people (month 7) your own company costs less each month than employer of record fees. Switching in month 7 pays back the setup cost by month 12.
results.money: You save about €58,200 over 24 months on fees and running costs, after paying for setup, compared with keeping everyone on employer of record, which the 18-month limit would not allow anyway. Salaries and employer taxes are the same on either route.
notes: You plan a long-term presence, which also points to your own company.
Running your own company costs 30% more here because you do not work in the local language.
hero_notes: German law limits each person to 18 months placed with you, counted from each person's start date. Your first hires would reach it in month 21, so employer of record could not cover them for the full 24 months.
Running your own company costs 30% more here because you do not work in the local language.
You plan a long-term presence, which also points to your own company.
steps: Month 3: hire your first 3 people through employer of record.
Month 4: start setting up your GmbH. It usually takes 6 to 12 weeks.
Month 7: move your team onto your own company.
flags: In Germany an employer of record must hold a labour leasing licence, and the same person can usually be placed with you for at most 18 months. The limit runs from each person's start date, and your first hires reach it in month 21.

review.summary: Use employer of record for your first hires, then move the team onto your own company from month 7, which is the recommended route for this plan. The switch pays back its setup cost by month 12 and saves €58,180 compared with keeping everyone on employer of record, which the 18 months per person limit would not allow for the full 24 months anyway.
review.driver: Every check points to your own company, and the financial check is the main driver because your own company becomes cheaper each month from 6 people. The long-term presence you plan also supports the move, and the 18 months per person limit is reached in month 21.
risks: An employer of record in Germany must hold a labour leasing licence, so confirm that any provider you use holds one before your first hires start in month 3.
Your first hires would reach the 18 months per person limit in month 21, so they must be moved before then to stay compliant.
Running your own company costs 30% more because you do not work in the local language, which adds to the ongoing cost once you switch.
